## Peer-reviewed articles

**Zimniak L, Soufiah E, [Ha CSR]{.underline}, Gretschel S, Paschold M.**
Improvement of mobility and motivation in patients with elective colorectal
resection using tracking devices and utilizing self-awareness (IMPETUS): a
randomized controlled trial in a traditional non-ERAS clinical setting.
*BMC Surgery* 2026;26(1).
[doi:10.1186/s12893-026-03864-6](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12893-026-03864-6)

: Third of five authors. As external consulting statistician I performed the a
  priori power calculation, contributed to the ethics-committee submission, and ran
  the primary-endpoint analysis in R.

**Gruebl T, Jungblut J, Rupp D, [Ha CSR]{.underline}, et al.**
The use of epinephrine in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a retrospective study of
the effects of administration timing and cumulative doses on outcome in a
physician-staffed emergency medical service system.
*BMC Emergency Medicine* 2025;25(1):182.
[doi:10.1186/s12873-025-01351-4](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-025-01351-4)

: Co-author. I restructured a single-table retrospective dataset into normalised
  relational tables, ran the statistical analysis, and contributed to the
  publication.

**Swojanowsky P, Bundis-Dimitrijevic M, [Ha CSR]{.underline}, von Korn H.**
Rationale and design of the VAST-AF trial: a randomized controlled, blinded,
clinical trial to evaluate transcutaneous vagal nerve stimulation for the prevention
of persistent atrial fibrillation recurrence.
*American Heart Journal* 2024;268:37–44.
[doi:10.1016/j.ahj.2023.11.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ahj.2023.11.015)

: Third of four authors. Statistical consulting on a randomised, controlled,
  double-blind trial in cardiology.

**[Ha CSR]{.underline}, Müller-Nurasyid M, Petrera A, Hauck SM, Marini F,
Bartsch DK, Slater EP, Strauch K.**
Proteomics biomarker discovery for individualized prevention of familial pancreatic
cancer using statistical learning.
*PLOS ONE* 2023;18(1):e0280399.
[doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0280399](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0280399)

: First author. An end-to-end machine-learning pipeline identifying early-detection
  biomarkers from next-generation proteomics in a pancreatic-cancer cohort, using
  model-based gradient boosting with stability selection for a high-dimensional,
  imbalanced design, validated with a dedicated simulation study.

## Manuscripts in preparation

**[Ha CSR]{.underline}, et al.**
A Metabolomics Approach to Familial Pancreatic Cancer: Discovering Early Diagnostic
Biomarkers through Machine Learning. *In preparation.*

: First author. Machine learning on LC-MS metabolomics for early detection, with a
  molecular interaction network constructed using Gaussian graphical models to
  reveal key interactions among compounds in high-risk individuals.
